title: Feelings
description: Say how you feel, and how other people feel.
grammar: adjectives that change, and the two verbs for how you are
grammarNote: An adjective that describes how you are goes after the verb estar, and it changes to match the person.

explanation.summary: Feelings are adjectives, and the ones that describe a temporary state go with estar: estoy feliz, está triste, están aburridos. The adjective changes its ending to match the person it describes.

sections.heading: The adjectives
sections.body: El happy one is feliz, and its feminine is feliz as well. The rest change: triste stays the same, aburrido becomes aburrida, enfadado becomes enfadada, tranquilo becomes tranquila, nervioso becomes nerviosa, contento becomes contenta, listo becomes lista, preocupado becomes preocupada and soñoliento becomes soñolienta.

sections.heading: Which verb to use
sections.body: The two verbs for what something is like both take an adjective, and the adjective comes after them. Ser is for what a thing is: el examen es difícil. Estar is for how a thing is now: estoy cansado. For feelings, it is estar that you want.

items.note: The same in both genders: estoy feliz, ella está feliz.
The same in both genders: está triste.
The feminine is aburrida: ella está aburrida.
The feminine es lista. It also means clever.
The feminine es soñolienta. The accent marks the stress.

drills.note: Feliz is the same in both genders.
The adjective changes to match the person.
